Done. The route now builds as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` with a complete static shell. **What changed** - `app/page.tsx` — now a sync component (no top-level `await`); static chrome (`

Dashboard

`) prerenders, and each section sits behind its own `` boundary so sections stream independently. - `app/data.ts` (new) — single fetch shared via `React.cache`, so the three sections dedupe to one request per render instead of blocking the page. - `app/CardStats.tsx`, `app/RevenueChart.tsx`, `app/LatestInvoices.tsx` — now async server components that await their own data, each with a matching `*Skeleton` export used as the fallback (headings included, so they're part of the shell and there's no layout shift). **Verified in the shell** (`.next/server/app/index.html`): contains `Dashboard`, all section headings, and 3 pending Suspense markers (``) with skeleton fallbacks inlined — previously the top-level `await` meant the shell had none of this. Data stays fresh per request (no `use cache`, per the docs' streaming-uncached-data pattern for dashboards). `app/loading.tsx` is now inert on direct visits since the page no longer suspends at the segment level; left in place as the route-segment fallback.
